text.p: U.S. T-bonds will struggle to make much headway on Tuesday, and any bounce will likely be temporary ahead of a move in the medium term down to the middle to upper 105s, technical analysts said.
"If the market can't stay above 106-25, things will be negative for today," said Donna Liu, technical analyst at DKB International here.
By 0902 GMT, the June T-bond was up 4/32 at 106-26.
"If we go below there, I'm looking for 106-12, then 106-00 before a move down to 105-12 which is equivalent to around 7.25 percent on the long bond," said Liu.
Analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell here agreed the market was looking for a new low in the mid to upper 105s, before a bounce.

"As long as bonds hold below 107-04, we should be able to sink back below Friday's 106-11 low en route to a bottom at least down at 105-27, with the 105-16 area a possible attractor," DMG said in a note.
Liu said that on the upside, if the market does manage to pierce 106-25 convincingly, it would run into further resistance at 107-00 then 107-08, an area of congestion.
"But overall I'd stay bearish -- any bounce will be temporary," she said.

Gerry Celaya, senior technical analyst at American Express Bank here, said the T-bond would face strong resistance at 107-12, a trendline which has marked the topside for the bond over the last few weeks.
"A sustained break higher, while difficult, would set the stage for 107-31 and 109 further out," he said in a note.
Markets will be pre-occupied with March consumer price data due at 1230 GMT.
According to a Reuter poll, economists expect the CPI to rise 0.2 percent in March from a 0.3 percent rise in February. Core CPI is seen up 0.3 percent, from 0.2 percent the previous month.
September Eurodollars were quoted at 93.645, unchanged in automated trade.
